[h1] This is a review for the entire Banner Saga series. [/h1]

The Banner Saga is an incredible series. Unlike many choice-driven games, the decisions you make actually carry weight. Small, seemingly meaningless choices can lead to massive consequences entire games later, making every decision feel tense and important.

The worldbuilding is deep and unique, supported by a compelling narrative that I honestly have never seen executed this well before. Combined with the gorgeous hand-drawn art style and fantastic soundtrack, the series creates an atmosphere that feels special.

[b] There are, however, two major flaws with the series: [/b]

[h3] Combat: [/h3]
The turn-based combat is both very fun and strangely designed at the same time. Damage is directly tied to a unit’s remaining health, and turns always alternate between you and the enemy. As a result, if you want to play “optimally,” you’re encouraged not to kill enemies immediately. Instead, the best tactic is to weaken every enemy to 1HP before finishing them off at the end. Otherwise, the strongest enemy units end up taking more turns.

It’s a very odd system for a tactics game and sometimes makes combat feel more like solving a math puzzle than making strategic battlefield decisions. Despite that, the combat is still enjoyable enough that I can mostly overlook the weirdness.


[h3] Banner Saga 3 Problems: [/h3]
This is the real issue with the series. Banner Saga 3 is plagued with bugs and crashes. I personally have a very high tolerance for bugs but it is almost unplayable.

Every loading screen feels like a gamble. I am not exaggerating when I say any time you encounter a loading screen, the game has a 1/4 chance of crashing/freezing. I had to replay a single battle FIVE TIMES just to make it past the post-fight loading screen. By the end, I probably had to redo nearly half the fights in the game at least once because of crashes.

What makes this even worse is that Banner Saga 3 contains multi-phase battles with additional loading screens in between. If the game had manual saves, this would be manageable. Instead, you are forced to keep rebooting the game and brute-forcing your way through until you finally get lucky.

The craziest part is that the first two games ran perfectly fine for me. Banner Saga 3 is not fundamentally different from them, which makes the state it was left in years after release feel completely unacceptable. 

The only reason I managed to push through Banner Saga 3 was because I was already deeply invested in the story and characters after the first two games.

TLDR: this game series is full of bugs (including GAME BREAKING bugs that appear only after you've bought the third game and spent more than 2 hours playing it so you can't refund it) and the developers are not providing meaningful support. DO NOT BUY. 

The deeper you get into the trilogy the buggier it gets. It gets really bad in BS2. Visuals bug out: scenes don't make sense because characters don't render when they're supposed to. Characters you've invested lots of resources in lose critical skills when you level them up for no apparent reason. Even worse these are known bugs that the developer has explicitly said they are not going to fix.

But then once you're $75 in and 3/4 of the way done with the story, the game-breaking bugs appear in BS3. FREQUENT crashes. Loading screens that never resolve. These are extra game-breaking because of how the save system works: there's no manual save, so if you spent 45 minutes completing a complex fight, and the game crashes--oops, now you have to redo it all! Even more maddening? You might have to do it a third time, a fourth time, or more! There's no way to know how many retries it'll take, or if it's just impossible to finish the game.

Even worse, the developers are just like, "oopsie, dunno why that happened! Join our Discord server where people are sharing weird workarounds like uninstalling the game and reinstalling it on an HDD!" 

Suffice to say I feel very ripped off.

The Banner Saga 3 delivers everything fans could hope for and more. It wraps up the epic story with emotional weight, high stakes, and the same stunning artistry that has defined the series. Every choice from the previous games matters, making your journey feel deeply personal and profoundly satisfying.

The combat is sharper and more tactical than ever. The addition of new abilities and thoughtful enemy design keeps battles tense, rewarding careful strategy and planning. Permadeath still carries weight, ensuring that every decision — both in and out of combat — feels meaningful.

Storytelling is where the finale shines brightest. Themes of leadership, sacrifice, and survival are handled with maturity and depth. Characters you’ve grown attached to face real consequences, making victories feel earned and losses sting in the best way. The narrative closure is heartfelt without being predictable, offering a fitting conclusion to the saga.

The art and soundtrack continue to be phenomenal, perfectly capturing the Viking-inspired world’s beauty, tension, and melancholy. Every frame feels deliberate, and every note of music complements the emotional tone.

The Banner Saga 3 is more than a game — it’s a saga in every sense of the word. For fans of strategy, storytelling, and emotionally rich worlds, it’s a perfect conclusion.

首先游戏标题的意思为：一面旗帜代表一个家族或文明的延续。人们将经历绣在旗帜上代代相传，只要旗帜还在，文明就不灭。

结局：在对抗黑裔指挥官时，鲁克或阿莱特其中一人可能会牺牲，存活者将成为第二部的主角。

[h3] Premise: [/h3]
Reviewing The Banner Saga is not easy without talking about the entire trilogy.
This is a saga where choices truly matter, and their consequences can echo from the first game all the way to the third. For this reason, I strongly recommend playing the trilogy by importing your saves from one game to the next, as this is where the series truly shines.

[h2] The Banner Saga 3: [/h2]
⚠️ Spoiler Warning: This section contains story and gameplay spoilers for The Banner Saga 3.

Unfortunately, this is the chapter I liked the least, and it frustrated me on more than one occasion.

The art direction remains inspired and well crafted, just like in the previous games, but the experience is far less exploratory, and most of its issues stem from this change.

At a certain point, management mechanics are completely removed, and I found many narrative choices frustrating. Several times I had to reload my last save because the consequences did not match what I reasonably expected, making choices feel almost random.

I really did not enjoy the Rook/Alette storyline. While the idea of trying to keep things under control after major events is interesting but spending the entire time inside a city felt extremely boring after two games where the journey itself was the core of the experience.

The journey of Juno, Eyvind, and Iver was more interesting but still very repetitive and not on par with the second chapter.

Combat is by far the most frustrating aspect of this game. The addition of Heroic Titles did not significantly improve gameplay, and the difficulty feels poorly balanced. Enemies are not truly difficult, they are simply long to kill. They have much higher strength and armor, making them disproportionate compared to your party.
The real challenge lies in weakening enemies fast enough to prevent them from one-shotting weaker party members (such as archers).

I played without engaging additional waves and never had issues with renown points. However, whenever I tried to push further, I was quickly defeated because I failed to kill all enemies before the round timer expired, causing reinforcements to arrive.

On top of that, I encountered several bugs that made the experience even more frustrating:
[list]
[*]The game once crashed during a loading screen after a battle. Since saving happens after combat, I had to replay the entire fight.
[*]On multiple occasions, at the start of a battle, I was unable to position my heroes due to a UI bug: I could click them, but not move them.
[*]Several times (including during the final battle), I was unable to confirm basic attacks. The only workaround was using abilities, which was extremely annoying, especially in the final fight, where I had to use Iver’s Tempest ability [*]I also noticed many translation and grammar errors in the Italian localization. While not game-breaking, these issues negatively impacted immersion and made the narrative feel less polished than expected, especially for such a story-driven game.
[/list]
Sadly, this third chapter disappointed me greatly and does not reflect the experience of the previous games. This is further worsened by the lack of a proper conclusion to Alette/Rook’s storyline, which feels unresolved unless the protagonist dies. While that post-death scene is very well done, the absence of an equivalent ending if the protagonist survives feels like a questionable design choice.

Would I recommend The Banner Saga 3?
Only to conclude the saga.
If this chapter had been the first one, I probably would not have continued the series at all.
